description: This working paper by Robert Huang and Matthew Kahn, NBER Working Paper 29900 (April 2022), analyses the carbon emissions of US urban public transit agencies, which spend billions of dollars a year on workers, capital and energy. Coverage: data for the nation's transit agencies from 2002 to 2019, benchmarked against transit agencies in Germany and the United Kingdom; the authors study energy efficiency trends, explain the variation across agencies, and present a new operating profits metric that incorporates each agency's annual total carbon emissions. They find that the sector has not significantly reduced its carbon footprint during a time of rising concern about climate change. Format and access: a working paper with a DOI (10.3386/w29900). Licence and cost: free to read on the NBER site; no licence stated. Caveats: an economics working paper; the abstract was the part read and the data source is not named in it. The agency efficiency comparisons can set baseline emission intensities for transit decarbonisation and climate policy models. It relates to the National Transit Database and TCRP Report 226 in the catalogue.
